{"confirmed":true,"evidence":[{"heading":"N2 instructions — Section C: How to increase the rent and give this notice","id":"7621f3cdfae14d92b5777d44f620edbd19bd2126d494dddfc68261583181ea29","text":"SECTION
C How to increase the rent and give this notice

The guideline for rent increases set by the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing
does not apply to tenants who live in rental units that are partially exempt from the RTA.
In these cases, the landlord can raise the rent by any amount.

You can increase the rent if at least 12 months have passed since the date of the last
rent increase or since the date the tenant moved into the rental unit. If the previous
tenant assigned the rental unit to the current tenant within the 12 months before the
increase date, you can increase the rent if at least 12 months have passed since the
previous tenant’s last rent increase.

You must give the tenant the Notice of Rent Increase at least 90 days before the date
you will increase the tenant’s rent.

There are many ways that you can give this notice to your tenant. You can:
 hand it directly to the tenant or to an adult in the rental unit,
 leave it in the tenant's mailbox or where mail is ordinarily delivered,

_____________________________________________________________________________________________________
Notice of Rent Increase Unit Partially Exempt – Form N2
2
 place it under the door of the rental unit or through a mail slot in the door,
 send it by fax to a fax machine where the tenant carries on business or to a fax
machine in their home,
 send it by courier, or
 send it by mail.

You cannot give the tenant this notice by posting it on the door of the tenant’s rental
unit."},{"heading":"N1 instructions — Section C: How to increase the rent and give this notice","id":"2b1ee1673d0822c0043a1ecac510f46fa7825cd4b495c907a6adcceb577c01bf","text":"SECTION
C How to increase the rent and give this notice

You can increase the rent if at least 12 months have passed since the date of the last
rent increase or since the date the tenant moved into the rental unit. If the previous
tenant assigned the rental unit to the current tenant within the 12 months before the
increase date, you can increase the rent if at least 12 months have passed since the
previous tenant’s last rent increase.

You must give the tenant the Notice of Rent Increase at least 90 days before the date
you will increase the tenant’s rent.

There are many ways that you can give this notice to your tenant. You can:
 hand it directly to the tenant or to an adult in the rental unit,
 leave it in the tenant's mailbox or where mail is ordinarily delivered,
 place it under the door of the rental unit or through a mail slot in the door,
 send it by fax to a fax machine where the tenant carries on business or to a fax
machine in their home,
 send it by courier, or
 send it by mail.

_____________________________________________________________________________________________________
Notice of Rent Increase – Form N1

2
You cannot give the tenant this notice by posting it on the door of the tenant’s rental
unit."},{"heading":"Increasing a tenant's rent","id":"6ebf013239401d00cc45d78657ddfba061ca9251b07c54795e6171d66b1e8b71","text":"Increasing a tenant's rent

In most cases, the rent can be increased if at least 12 months have passed since the tenant first moved in or since the tenant's last rent increase.

A landlord must give at least 90 days' notice in writing of any rent increase. The proper forms for this notice (Form N1, N2 or N3) are available from the LTB."},{"heading":"Rules for rent increase","id":"ef2c8278e771d0c5485f4ed65142dbdde28e0ffd29163920c27e96b4c9f30509","text":"Rules for rent increase

In most cases, the rent for a residential unit can be increased if at least 12 months have passed since the:

last rent increase, or

date the tenancy began

The landlord must give a tenant written notice of a rent increase in the proper form at least 90 days before it takes effect.

The proper forms for this notice are available from the Landlord and Tenant Board. If your landlord has not provided the proper notice, or you believe that your rent has been raised by an improper amount, you can dispute it at the Landlord and Tenant Board within 12 months after the amount was first charged."},{"heading":"N1 instructions — Section B: When to use a different notice","id":"ef832f209b0ddce5e6d3d7d1172f5781b55cc9699aeb569c88ee258082bfa41e","text":"SECTION
B When to use a different notice

Most landlords must use this form (Form N1) when increasing the rent. However, there
are three exceptions:

• Use Form N2 to increase the tenant’s rent if the rental unit is exempt from the
rules under the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 (the RTA) limiting the amount of
the rent increase.
• Use Form N3 (Notice to Increase the Rent and/or Charges for Care Services and
Meals) if the rental unit is in a care home.
• Use Form N10 if you and the tenant have agreed to increase the rent above the
guideline because you:
 have done or will do capital work, or
 have provided or will provide a new or additional service."}],"facts":{"current_cents":100000,"effective_on":"2026-09-01","form":"N1","guideline_status":"controlled","last_increase":{"date":null,"state":"none"},"proposed_cents":102100,"scope":{"ordinary":"confirmed","period_start":"confirmed"},"served_on":"2026-06-03","service_method":"hand","tenancy_start":"2025-09-01"},"mode":"rent"}
